As Apple continues to expand its Car Keys feature across the automotive industry, the feature now appears to be coming to select models from a major Chinese carmaker. Here are the details.

Apple Wallet's Car Keys reportedly set to support GWM Tank

According to findings by MacRumors, new backend code suggests Apple may soon be extending its Car Keys feature in Apple Wallet to GWM (Great Wall Motors) Tank series vehicles.

Several GWM models already support Apple CarPlay, including the Tank 300, Tank 400, Tank 500 and Tank 700, as well as models from its Haval, Ora, Wey and Poer brands.

However, none of these vehicles currently support the Car Keys feature, which allows drivers to use their iPhone or Apple Watch to lock, unlock and start compatible vehicles.

Just days before this news broke, new backend code had indicated that the Car Keys feature would be coming to Volkswagen vehicles. Apple has been steadily expanding its support following recent rollouts for brands including Toyota and Rivian.

Apple announced in 2025 that 13 automotive brands would be joining the ranks of Car Keys supporters, including GWM's Wey, as well as Acura, Cadillac, Chery, Chevrolet, GMC, Hongqi, Lucid, Porsche, Rivian, Smart, Tata Motors and Voyah.

According to Apple's official website, more than 800 vehicle models currently support CarPlay, of which 52 also support the Car Keys feature. Click here for the full compatibility list.
